title: Gemini 4 Argon API Pricing: Tokens and Search (2026)
summary: Gemini 4 Argon API pricing is unconfirmed for 2026 with no verified per-token rates. Check whether Google has announced any official pricing.
body_markdown:
## Worked cost of 1,000 automation runs


$7.00 buys a thousand email summaries on Gemini 4 Argon, while a cheaper Gemini Flash model does the same thousand for about $2.63, making email summaries a domain where model choice saves substantial money.


A thousand ticket classifications cost $1.20 versus $0.45, and classifications thereby become another task where model choice drives costs significantly.


According to Google[Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing) , Argon costs[$2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens](https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing) , against $0.75 and $3.75 for the Flash model. Both rates run at 37.5% of Argon's, so every step costs about 2.7 times more on Argon.


### Gemini 4 Argon cost of summarising an email


I assume 2,000 input tokens (a long thread) and 300 output tokens (a summary). On Argon that's $0.004 in plus $0.003 out, or $0.007 per run, so $7.00 per 1,000. On Flash it's $0.0015 plus $0.001125, about $2.63 per 1,000.


Make the summary chattier and the bill grows, though input is still the larger share of it.


I assume 500 input tokens and a 20-token label for classifying a support ticket. Argon costs $0.001 in plus $0.0002 out, so $1.20 per 1,000. Flash costs $0.000375 plus $0.000075, so $0.45 per 1,000.


Output is tiny here, so input length sets the price, and trimming the ticket text saves more than shortening the answer.


### Gemini 4 Argon monthly cost at scale


Multiply by volume and the gap moves from cents to hundreds of dollars, whether you run 1,000, 10,000 or 100,000 runs a month, because at scale these per-task differences become major spending drivers.


At 100,000 runs, summaries cost $700 on Argon and $262.50 on Flash, so at volume your model choice alone determines whether this task costs under $300 or approaches $700 monthly. Classification costs $120 versus $45.

Send a classifier to Argon and you spend $75 a month more for a label, and a classifier rarely needs Argon's reasoning.
